SWEEP 1 RESULT — PAID-DEMAND EVIDENCE (verified live 2026-08-01)

## Method note: can OpenRouter free vs paid be split?
- OpenRouter publishes NO paid/free traffic split. Rankings and model-page "Activity" charts mix variants; the public frontend JSON API that once exposed per-model stats now returns HTML (locked down, verified today). Model-page token charts render client-side only.
- The workable proxy: `:free` routes are **separate model IDs**, so a model's paid volume is clean **only if no :free route exists**. Checked live via `GET openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` (336 models, 2026-08-01): **none of GLM-5.2, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Flash, or Hy3 has a :free variant today** (14 :free models exist: Nemotron, Gemma-4, Ling, Laguna, gpt-oss-20b — none of our four). So *current* OpenRouter traffic on all four is paid-per-token. *Historical* July rankings are polluted (see Hy3).
- OpenRouter's own methodology note (blog "DeepSeek V4 Is Earning Agentic Token Share", data Jan 1–Jun 14 2026, 450T tokens): share figures are token share, NOT spend share, and they explicitly flag the two "diverge sharply for low-cost models like V4." Grade any raw OpenRouter token ranking: **UNRELIABLE as a paid-demand metric on its own.**

## Hy3 (control — tencent/hy3) — owner's suspicion CONFIRMED
- `tencent/hy3:free` existed as a **promo route Jul 6–Jul 21 2026** (TechTimes 2026-07-13; APIRank tutorial; ayautomate). During that window "Hy3 free version" topped OpenRouter weekly usage at **613B tokens/wk** (KuCoin flash, ~Jul 10). That headline volume was the free variant.
- Verified today: `tencent/hy3:free` endpoints = **0** (dead route); paid `tencent/hy3` has only **5 endpoints** (Tencent, DeepInfra, Novita, GMICloud, AtlasCloud) at $0.13–0.14/$0.53–0.58, currently 8% off (discount = demand-stimulation, not demand). Kilo still lists a `tencent-hy3-free` route on its own platform.
- Post-free-window paid provider count (5, vs 22–33 for V4 Flash/GLM-5.2) is the cleanest signal: **paid capacity did NOT follow the free-window volume.** Grade: **HIGH confidence that Hy3's July volume fame was free-tier pollution; weak paid demand.**

## GLM-5.2 (z-ai/glm-5.2, released ~Jun 13 2026, MIT)
- **33 OpenRouter endpoints** (most of any model checked; live API today): Z.AI first-party $1.40/$4.40, plus Fireworks, Together, DeepInfra, Baseten, Novita, Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, CoreWeave, SiliconFlow, Alibaba, Baidu, Friendli, Phala, Venice, etc. Grade: **HIGH** (provider count = capacity following paid demand; DO/Cloudflare = enterprise distribution).
- **GLM Coding Plan (subscription)**: live tiers **Lite $18 / Pro $72 / Max $160 per month**, 30% intro promo ($12.60) — z.ai/subscribe + aipricing.guru (updated within hours of today) + docs.z.ai devpack (off-peak credits, "save up to 92% vs GLM-5.2 on-demand"). Plan "went viral in North America," promo price **doubled Feb 11 2026** due to demand (remio.ai, 2026-04-16). Grade: **HIGH** (price *raised* = real willingness-to-pay).
- Revenue: JPMorgan raised Zhipu 2026–2030 forecasts 7–16% after ZCode launch, projecting **>534% 2026 revenue surge**, profit by 2028 (VentureBeat, ~Jul 2026); Zhipu is HK-listed (Caixin) — audited paid revenue exists. 2025 revenue +132% (theairankings, 2026-06-19). Grade: **HIGH.**
- Agent-platform: z.ai/subscribe explicitly targets Claude Code, Kilo Code, Cline, OpenCode; Kilo (3M+ devs, paid tokens) features GLM-5.2 in its reviewed model feed (kilo.ai/open-source-models, 2 days old). Kilo Bench 53.0% at $26.21/attempt. Grade: **MEDIUM-HIGH.**
- Note for the 8xH100 premise: Pinggy (2026-07-27) calls GLM-5.2 "the leader among models that fit a single node."

## Kimi K3 (moonshotai/kimi-k3, launched Jul 16–17 2026, weights Jul 27, Modified MIT, 2.8T params)
- **Strongest first-party paid signal of the three**: Moonshot ARR **$200M (April) → $300M (June/July)**; K3 launch drove **>6x daily subscription sales**, forcing a **pause on new sign-ups Jul 18–19** (Caixin Global 2026-07-21; cryptobriefing; BigGo). Valuation toward $50B / HK IPO (Startup Fortune, ~Jul 24). Grade: **HIGH** — demand literally exceeded capacity.
- API: first-party $3.00 in / $0.30 cached / $15.00 out per 1M (Moonshot official, corroborated by OpenRouter, requesty, benchlm — all ≤2 days old). Premium pricing tier — every token is expensive, so its OpenRouter presence is high-spend by construction.
- Consumer/coding subscriptions: Kimi app tiers free–$199/mo; $99 "Allegro" tier reportedly matches Anthropic's $200 plan on coding quota (emergent.sh, 4 days ago). Wikipedia (1 wk old): ~$20M monthly revenue reference; China tiers 5.2–399 yuan.
- **Only 10 OpenRouter endpoints** and shakier serving (DigitalOcean + one Fireworks route status −2/degraded uptime today) — the 2.8T size limits who can host it. Capacity growth is the constraint, not appetite. Grade: **HIGH paid demand, MEDIUM serving breadth.**
- Kilo Bench: best OSS score, 72.8% completion, but $48.38/attempt. r/cursor users actively demanding K3/GLM-5.2 integration (1 wk old) — not yet a Cursor default.

## DeepSeek V4 Flash (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, released Apr 24 2026; 0731 re-post-train added Jul 31, MIT)
- **22 endpoints** on the base model; the **0731 revision, one day old, already has 8 providers** (DeepInfra, GMICloud, Fireworks, Cloudflare, DeepSeek, Parasail, AtlasCloud, SiliconFlow) — fastest capacity-follow observed. Grade: **HIGH.**
- OpenRouter's own insights blog (data through Jun 14): DeepSeek ~doubled token share (9%→18%), **top model on OpenRouter since mid-May**, and critically the growth is **agentic-keyed traffic** (their 7-signal API-key classifier): by end of May **V4-Flash = 70% of DeepSeek agentic token flow**. Agentic API-key traffic is real production usage, and DeepSeek has no :free route — this volume is paid, just cheaply paid ($0.14/$0.28 list; $0.09/$0.18 cheapest endpoint). Explicit caveat from OpenRouter: token share ≠ spend share. Grade: **HIGH volume / MEDIUM revenue-intensity.**
- First-party capacity-constraint signal: DeepSeek API docs (live today) announce **peak/off-peak pricing with 2x peak prices** — you don't ration peak capacity without paying demand. Responses API shipped for v4-flash *first* (v4-pro "early August") — Flash is their volume workhorse. Grade: **HIGH.**
- No subscription product; no usage disclosures beyond the above. Enterprise distribution: Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Baidu, Alibaba all serve it.

## Cross-cutting
- **Fast-silicon providers**: Groq serves only `kimi-k2-instruct` (old K2; verified on console.groq.com today); Cerebras serves only `zai-glm-4.7` among Chinese models, deprecating Aug 17 2026 (inference-docs.cerebras.ai, live) — successor unannounced. None of the three candidates is on wafer/LPU silicon yet; the paid capacity race is on GPU clouds.
- **Coding-agent defaults**: nothing ships as a hard *default* in Cursor/Windsurf yet (reasoning-format friction cited on r/cursor). The paid-token channel that matters is BYO-key/subscription harnesses: Kilo/Cline/Claude Code/OpenCode, where GLM Coding Plan and Kimi's coding tiers are first-class integrations. Kilo's usage-ranked leaderboard (paid tokens, 3M devs) currently features GLM-5.2, Kimi K3, Qwen3-Coder, Laguna in its model feed; its FAQ names step-3.7-flash top by usage today.

## Bottom line (paid-demand ranking)
1. **Kimi K3** — hardest evidence: ARR $200M→$300M in 2 months, 6x subscription surge, sign-up pause. Constraint: 2.8T weights = thin third-party hosting (10 endpoints, some degraded).
2. **DeepSeek V4 Flash** — largest paid token volume (agentic-keyed, no free route, top of OpenRouter since mid-May; 22+8 endpoints; first-party peak-pricing rationing), but lowest $/token so revenue-share understates nothing for *us* — for darklanes it's the volume/serving-efficiency play.
3. **GLM-5.2** — broadest paid distribution (33 endpoints), audited listed-company revenue trajectory, subscription price *raised* under demand; strongest "fits one node" fit for an 8xH100 unit.
4. **Hy3 (control)** — CONFIRMED polluted: July volume fame = 15-day :free promo (ended Jul 21, route now dead, 0 endpoints); only 5 paid providers followed. Weak paid demand.

Owner's shortlist priors: **confirmed** — the three candidates are exactly where paid signals concentrate; Hy3 skepticism validated.

## 4. Verdicts — where margin structurally lives

- **GLM-5.2: the only candidate where vanilla economics close.** Published SGLang throughput (733) already beats the median-price BE on any node ≤$24/hr (460), and beats it at capacity-block cost if you push concurrency past Phala's c=16. At FLOOR prices on AWS CB it is dead (need 1,525 vs 733 published) — floor sellers are on cheap/owned capacity. Margin = median-or-official pricing + sub-$25 nodes + prefix caching + the fast-lane premium (Fireworks/Wafer/BaseTen "fast" lanes sell at $2.10/$6.60 = 1.5x). This is darklanes' natural target: single node, W4AFP8, MTP works (our engine's strong suit).
- **Kimi K3: fattest per-token revenue, gated on multi-node capability — that IS the moat.** BE of ~930 out tok/s across 3 nodes (~310/node) is modest for the price charged; the floor sits at 97% of official because almost nobody can serve 1.68TB. Risk: active-params reports conflict (32B–104B); at 104B active, decode cost/token is ~2.6x DeepSeek-V3-class. If darklanes can do 3-node EP serving, K3 is where margin lives; if the one-8xH100-node premise is hard, K3 is out of scope.
- **DeepSeek V4 Flash: dead at floor prices, near-dead at median, on rented H100s.** Median-price BE (8.2k out tok/s @ CB, 4.8k @ $24) requires DeepSeek-grade disagg infra just to break even, and DeepSeek's own $0.0028 cache price plus incoming peak-hour 2x pricing says even they are margin-thin. Serving V4F profitably = winning an infra-efficiency race against its author on commodity pricing. Only plays: cache-read arbitrage (charge $0.018–0.07 for near-zero-cost tokens) and latency premium (Makora sells 268 t/s output).

## 5. Subscription angle (live prices)

- **GLM Coding Plan** (z.ai/subscribe, docs.z.ai, aipricing.guru Aug 1): Lite **$18/mo** (~80 prompts/5h, 400/wk), Pro **$72** (5x Lite), Max **$160** (20x), 30% promo from $12.60. **Kimi plans** (Moonshot, lorphic/geotoolbox Jul 2026): **$19/$39/$99/$199**/mo tempo-named tiers.
- Subscriptions invert the floor problem: an $18–$160 cap-limited seat monetizes far above per-token floors. Darklanes seat math on GLM-5.2 @ ~730–900 out tok/s/node = 8–10 saturated concurrent streams: a $24/hr node costs $17.3k/mo → **~240 Pro-tier ($72) seats/node = 24–30x oversubscription**, which is exactly what 5–10% active duty cycles + admission control + session-affinity prefix caching deliver; Lite-tier ($18) needs ~100x oversub, viable only with Z.ai-style hard 5-hour caps. On the $41.5 CB node the same product needs ~415 Pro seats — subscriptions want cheap or owned capacity too.
- What the darklanes product must deliver per seat: 50–120 tok/s decode when active (matches our measured 131 tok/s/stream class), burst admission within ~1s, prefix-cache hit on multi-turn (our v2 gap list already names session affinity + admission control as the exact missing pieces).

**Bottom line:** GLM-5.2 = viable per-token business at median prices on ≤$25/hr nodes and the best subscription substrate; Kimi K3 = highest structural margin if (and only if) we take on 3-node serving; DeepSeek V4 Flash = commodity knife-fight, only cache/latency arbitrage survives. ## 3. K3 special case — exact requirements

- Needs **1,560.94GB for weights alone** (MXFP4 QAT native; MXFP8 would be ~2.8TB, BF16 ~5.6TB — neither released). 
- Viable configs today: **8x B300 (2,304GB, single node, native FP4)** ← intended target; 16x B200 (2 nodes, DP16+EP16, 56 experts/GPU); 16x H200 (2 nodes, TP16+EP16, marlin, ~103GB/GPU — leaves only ~8GB KV/GPU); 32x H100 (4 nodes, 28 experts/GPU, ~3.6GB KV/GPU — evals only).
- **8xH100: nothing works** — no offload story either (69 KDA layers hold per-request recurrent state; standard prefix caching only covers the 24 MLA layers).
- On all Hopper it pays the W4A16 marlin dequant tax; Hopper has no FP4 tensor cores. vLLM support not yet in main; SGLang `lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3` image is the working engine.

## 4. Latency/UX floor — what paid users actually get (OpenRouter per-endpoint tables, read live today)

**DeepSeek V4 Flash** (22 endpoints, $0.09-0.14/M in, $0.18-0.28/M out): Fireworks **105 tps**, Baidu 87, AtlasCloud 83, Alibaba 82, DeepSeek-official 65, SiliconFlow 63, Parasail 59, Novita 54 — bulk of endpoints 20-60 tps; latency 0.65-2.2s. Paid token share is spread wide (Baidu 19.3%, Novita 17.5%, StreamLake 13.4%, DeepSeek 11.9%) — a real multi-provider paid market at commodity prices.

**GLM-5.2** ($1.40/$4.40 std, $2.10/$6.60 "Fast" tier): Baseten Fast **187 tps**, Fireworks Fast 160, CoreWeave 145, Ionstream 136, Cloudflare Fast 131, Wafer Fast 103 — standard endpoints mostly 30-90 tps, Z.ai itself 54 tps @3.0s latency. The paid "Fast tier" market (customers paying 1.5x for speed) shows single-stream speed is monetizable here. Token share: CoreWeave 21.7%, Baidu 15.4%, Decart 14.0%.

**Kimi K3** ($3/$15; $4.50/$22.50 Fast): Fireworks Fast **79 tps**, Modal 73, Baseten 62, Fireworks 54, Together 49, Moonshot-official only **23 tps @4.87s** latency; Moonshot holds 67.2% of paid token share, third parties struggle (Fireworks std uptime 81.5%). ## 2. Parallelism forms ranked by ENGINEERING DISTANCE for memra

**Rank 1 — PIPELINE parallel (shortest): ~2-3 weeks to a gated 8-stage MVP.**
What it touches: (i) a layer-range loader (`hybrid.rs:677 load_from_source` gains `layer_range: Range<usize>`; GGUF tensors are loaded by per-layer name so range-load is a filter; embed table on stage 0, `output_norm`+`output`+sampler on last stage); (ii) a stage worker = today's `worker.rs` pattern instantiated per ordinal (one process per GPU, exactly like the darklanes replicas); (iii) a ring protocol: ship `x` (`4*n_embd` bytes ≈ 16-32KB/token/hop) forward, 4-byte token id back to stage 0. Kernels: **zero changes**. Cache: each stage allocates `Some` only for its range (structure already supports it, memra-kv:131). CUDA graphs: capture per-stage bodies unchanged; NCCL send/recv is graph-capturable (or run comms eager between graph replays first).
What breaks / needs work: microbatch pipelining in the scheduler (pipe is full only with ≥ n_stages in-flight microbatches — at darklanes concurrency c=16-64 this holds; single-stream decode leaves 7/8 GPUs idle per tick); prefill pipelines naturally in `PREFILL_TICK_T` chunks (`worker.rs:38`); spec/MTP verify rounds pay the ring latency once per round (~8 × 10-20µs — noise vs multi-ms steps of a 300-750B model); per-stage layer-time balancing (MoE layers dominate — balance by expert-bytes not layer count).
Exactness: same kernels, same FP order, f32 activations in transit → **bit-identical to single-GPU is achievable by construction**, so the argmax/spec gates carry over.

**Rank 2 — EXPERT parallel + DP attention (medium): ~3-5 weeks on top of the comms layer.**
What it touches: deep surgery in ONE module — `hybrid_forward.rs` MoE dispatch. After routing (sel/w already computed, host or device), partition token×expert pairs by owner rank (a shard-aware variant of the existing expert-major CSR grouping at `hybrid_forward.rs:3121`), all-to-all activations out / partials back (NCCL grouped send/recv), deterministic slot-ordered combine (the existing sequential-axpy bit-identity class). `DevExps` becomes the local shard (n_expert/8 experts) + a global-id→(rank,slot) table — same fused `_dev`/pairs/gdec kernels, just a smaller pointer row. The trunk (attention, norms, shared expert, lm_head) stays **replicated per GPU with per-replica sessions — which is literally darklanes' existing replica-per-GPU + proxy structure**. This is why EP is rank 2 and not rank 1: the server/session model is reused wholesale; only the expert FFN gets a cross-GPU hop.
Cost model: per MoE layer per token, ≤2 × top_k × n_embd × 4B ≈ 0.5MB → ~25-40MB/token across 60-90 layers → ~2ms at 450GB/s effective NVLink; amortized across the batch per all-to-all. This is the known EP tax; DeepEP/NVSHMEM exists to shrink it at scale — irrelevant single-node v1.
Exactness: expert matvec FP chains unchanged; fixed combine order preserves bit-identity. Router stays replicated (each replica routes its own tokens) — no divergence risk.

**Rank 3 — TENSOR parallel (rewrite-class): 6-10+ weeks, not recommended.**
Every projection in every arm — mmvq/mma fatbins, cuBLASLt calls, CUTLASS FFI (`cutlass_ffi.rs`), MMQ (`mmq_ffi.rs`), fused epilogues, dp4a expert kernels — needs sharded weights + partial-sum epilogue + 2 allreduces per layer. It also **breaks the exactness contract** (split-K reduction order changes every logit), forcing a re-baseline of the argmax/spec gate battery, which is memra's core discipline. Only justified if single-stream latency on the dense trunk must scale or attention weights are too big to replicate — neither holds for these MoE candidates (active params are small; MLA/GQA attention weights are a few GB).

## 3. The pragmatic hybrid (verified against live docs)

vLLM Expert Parallel Deployment doc (docs.vllm.ai, page dated **2026-07-28**, fetched 2026-08-01): canonical single-node DeepSeek-class config is `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel` — **attention replicated per GPU (DP), experts sharded EP8**; TP>1 only when attention won't fit/latency demands; `EP_SIZE = TP×DP`. EPLB for skew; DeepEP/NVSHMEM only for multi-node. SGLang DeepSeek doc (docs.sglang.ai, fetched 2026-08-01): `--enable-dp-attention --tp 16 --dp 2` on 2 nodes — same shape, DP attention + big EP group.
**Implication: the industry-standard endpoint for these models is exactly "memra's existing replica-per-GPU trunk + a sharded expert bank" — memra is unusually well-positioned for EP, and TP is skippable.**
Minimal viable memra version: **PP-only first is competitive on aggregate throughput** — decode is weight-stream-bound; PP8 with a full pipe streams every GPU's layer weights continuously (8× aggregate HBM, no allreduce), matching TP8-class aggregate at serving batch sizes; it loses ~n_stages× on single-stream latency and amortizes expert reads worse than EP's global-batch grouping (llama.cpp's `--split-mode layer` is the weak version of this — no microbatch overlap; memra's step-interleave scheduler already has the microbatch structure to beat it). PP bubbles die in steady-state continuous decode (no flushes); they only appear at prefill admission — chunked prefill (already present) fills them.

# DARKLANES 8xH100 PRODUCTION SERVING — DECISION + BUILD PLAN (synthesized 2026-08-01)

## 1. THE PICK: GLM-5.2

The owner's shortlist survives contact with the evidence, but only one of the three wins on all three axes at once.

**Elimination first:**

- **Kimi K3 is a hard physical no on the production unit.** 1,560.94 GB MXFP4 weights (the QAT release IS the 4-bit floor; nothing smaller exists) against 640 GB HBM. Minimum Hopper deployment is 4x 8xH100 nodes at 5.8 tok/s single-stream, or 2x 8xH200 at 146.9 tok/s aggregate. It has the strongest paid-demand evidence of anything checked (ARR $200M→$300M in two months, sign-up pause under load, 97% floor/official price — no price competition because almost nobody can host 1.68 TB) — which makes it the correct *phase-2 multi-node* target, not the build target. Parking it is a scope decision, not a demand verdict.
- **DeepSeek V4 Flash fits the node best and loses the economics worst.** It is the only clean 8xH100 fit (~167 GB, two replicas per node) and has the largest paid agentic token volume on OpenRouter. But break-even at *median* paid prices is 4,762 out tok/s per $24/hr node (8,234 at our capacity-block cost), and the only existence proof that such numbers are reachable is DeepSeek's own disaggregated multi-node infra. DeepSeek's $0.0028 cache price and incoming 2x peak-hour pricing say the author itself is margin-thin. Serving V4F is an infra-efficiency knife-fight against its creator at commodity prices. Not a business for a new entrant.
- **GLM-5.2 is where demand, economics, and our engineering advantage intersect:**
  - *Paid demand:* 33 paid OpenRouter endpoints (most of any model checked), audited HK-listed revenue with a >534% 2026 forecast raise (JPMorgan), and — the strongest signal — the Coding Plan subscription price was **raised** under demand. A paid "Fast tier" market exists at 1.5x ($2.10/$6.60) proving single-stream speed is directly monetizable, which is memra's measured strength.
  - *Node economics:* the only candidate where the math closes. Median-price break-even is 460 out tok/s on a $24/hr node; the published anchor is 733 out tok/s (8xH200, W4AFP8, c=16, EAGLE MTP). Subscriptions close harder: ~240 Pro-tier ($72/mo) seats per $24/hr node at 24–30x oversubscription, which is exactly what admission control + session affinity + 5–10% duty cycles deliver — and admission is the fleet layer darklanes already built.
  - *The structural moat:* the entire official GLM-5.2 ecosystem starts at 8xH200 (FP8 = ~744 GB; H100 is absent from every vLLM/SGLang recipe). memra's native GGUF Q4 path (~400–420 GB) puts it on the cheaper 8xH100 tier that no official recipe supports — and memra serves quantized weights through its own mmvq/MMQ kernels natively rather than paying the W4A16-marlin-dequant tax the community AWQ path pays. ## 2. THE BUILD PLAN

**Architecture endpoint (from sweep 3's ranking, confirmed against live vLLM/SGLang docs):** DP-attention + Expert Parallel, TP=1. The industry-standard single-node config for this model class (`--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel`) is structurally "darklanes' existing replica-per-GPU trunk + a sharded expert bank." memra is unusually well-positioned for exactly this shape. TP is explicitly deferred: rewrite-class (6–10+ weeks), touches every GEMM arm, and breaks the exactness contract by changing reduction order — and the verified industry endpoint doesn't need it.

**What carries over (verified in-repo):**
- Per-ordinal, thread-affine engine (`Engine::new(ordinal)`, lib.rs:683) — the stage/replica worker is a clone of the existing `worker.rs` pattern.
- Step-interleave scheduler + batched decode tick (B≤8, bit-exact tier) — the microbatch structure PP needs already exists.
- Per-layer `Vec<Option<KvLayer>>` KV cache — stages allocate only their layer range with zero structural change.
- MoE dispatch machinery (expert-major CSR grouping, `DevExps` per-layer slabs + pointer rows) — the natural EP shard unit; EP is surgery in one module (`hybrid_forward.rs`), not a rewrite.
- **Spec/MTP strength:** GLM-5.2 ships a native MTP layer with 5 draft tokens. memra's MTP machinery (1.35–1.76x measured) is the direct lever on both the 733 aggregate anchor (Phala's number includes EAGLE MTP) and the Fast-tier single-stream market (103–187 tps paid lanes).
- **Exactness gates carry by construction:** PP ships f32 residuals between unchanged kernels — bit-identical to single-GPU is achievable, so kernel-check/run-gen/run-spec transfer. EP preserves bit-identity via fixed slot-ordered combine. This is the discipline advantage no competitor engine has.
- Admission proxy + pair-packing fleet layer (the darklanes 1,480 tok/s 3xH100 result) — becomes the DP-attention front and the subscription seat-management layer.
- GGUF quant pipeline — the node-fit enabler itself.
